reasoning_and_instruction: Return, payoff, simple growth and before/after-fee terminology are separated. Positive starting wealth, equal model-year periods and endpoint distribution assumptions are explicit.
Reinvested distributions purchase actual fractional shares; retaining distributions at zero yield is a distinct policy. End-date reinvestment changes share count without changing endpoint wealth.

Compounding and annualization reproduce realized growth rather than forecast it. Arithmetic means, geometric means, expected wealth and expected log wealth are distinguished; independence and finite expectations are stated where needed.

Logs require positive wealth. A total loss has no finite log, and financed negative equity cannot be continued as an ordinary positive-wealth index. Time additivity does not imply cross-asset log averaging; Jensen uses nonnegative weights and specifies equality.

True TWR splits at every external-flow valuation. Investor IRR uses all signed dated cash, with a monotonic positive-root proof only for the restricted contribution fixture. Missing intermediate valuations do not identify true TWR. The separate binding-capital-call exercise correctly has two roots.

Modified Dietz uses gain excluding contributions divided by time-weighted capital. Its cumulative horizon, approximation and problematic denominator are explicit; it is not relabeled as true TWR or an annual IRR.

The fee model specifies entry, post-market management and pre-redemption bases. Currency conversion follows actual quote units; real purchasing power divides by the price-level factor. Fictional terminal taxes use separate income and realized-gain bases.

The portfolio identity closes the beginning-wealth budget including signed financing. The repaired opportunity-set paragraph normalizes each per-unit payoff by price before using wealth weights. Physical probabilities are not asserted to be pricing probabilities.

All state inequalities are intersected with long-only bounds. A tighter floor activates the previously nonbinding up-state lower bound. Hindsight winner selection and end-of-period weights are not treated as feasible prior decisions.
Buy-and-hold weights drift from actual holdings; target rebalancing is self-financing and path-dependent. The exercise reverses its performance ranking, preventing a universal superiority claim.

Every required exercise method is taught before use. Eight complete solutions match their actual prompts. The open reporting critique grades timing, feasible decisions and evidence, not a preferred investment opinion. Teach-back has the worked reconstruction and explicit success criterion; three delayed-retention answers are supplied.

resolved_findings.finding: The original convex-hull sentence used raw asset payoff vectors even though earlier definitions permitted unequal purchase prices. Wealth weights require fixed-budget normalized payoffs.
resolved_findings.resolution: Coordinator changed the sentence to convex combinations of W0 X_i/P_i,0, equivalently asset-return vectors, and explicitly distinguished raw per-unit payoffs. Re-read final paragraph and verified independently with unequal asset prices; preceding equations and all lab cases were already correct. Final author record records the repair.

limitations: Independent agent review is not external academic or human certification and cannot guarantee the absence of every error.
Synthetic finite cases are not authenticated market records, investment advice, tax law or a GIPS compliance assessment.

The cash-flow solver is intentionally bounded to the documented annual contribution case. The review does not validate arbitrary IRR streams, irregular-day calendars, all malformed JSON types or extreme floating-point magnitudes.
Structural/offline numerical checks do not substitute for browser visual, keyboard, mobile or print review; those shared acceptance gates remain coordinator-owned.
